note: Two offline planning scenarios for connection reuse, SQL execution choices, current saved-query limitations, and Airflow SDK deployment. Give a fresh evaluator the full skill and one prompt, without expected_output or assertions. Do not execute platform operations. Assess every assertion against the resulting answer; these cases require human or model judgement and do not prove live API behavior.

evals.name: transfer-discovery-and-saved-analysis
evals.prompt: We use DLP and already have a PostgreSQL connection in workbook Sources. Its SQL read access setting has not been checked. Plan a Copy transfer into our lakehouse: discover the source tables and choose incremental cursors and initial values. The orders table has update_dt populated on every change; events is append-only with a monotonically increasing id; signups is append-only with create_dt. We need the full available history on the first load. I also want an ad-hoc SQL analysis saved in workbook Analysis. Explain the prerequisites, distinguishing a connection owned by Sources from a shared connection stored in a collection and linked into Sources. Do not call APIs or change resources.
evals.expected_output: Verify SQL read access, reuse the configured connection to inspect source tables, and select suitable cursors. Leave initialState unset for the requested full-history first load. Copy a workbook-owned connection into Analysis, or link the same shared collection connection with the required permissions; then save the analysis and run it by ID through runSqlQuery or its documented SDK equivalent.

assertions.text: Checks that SQL read access is enabled before inspecting data or running the saved analysis, and reuses the existing PostgreSQL connection to inspect tables, columns, and data through SQL.
Selects update_dt for mutable orders and considers id and create_dt for the append-only tables.
Leaves initialState empty/unset for the requested full-history first load, explaining that copying starts at the earliest available value; does not require an explicit starting cursor.

Copies a connection owned by Sources into Analysis. If Sources links a shared connection in a collection, links that same shared object into Analysis with the required permissions; does not propose directly linking an ordinary workbook-owned connection.
Chooses a saved DataLens SQL query and /rpc/runSqlQuery by query ID, or the documented SDK equivalent; does not assume an external PostgreSQL connection supplies a Trino coordinator.

evals.name: git-etl-and-temporary-trino-sql
evals.prompt: We are setting up a reliable DLP Airflow ETL pipeline. A SQL file containing CREATE TABLE followed by INSERT will be reviewed and versioned in Git, and we do not want saved DataLens query objects for each run. We also need to execute an occasional temporary Trino diagnostic without saving it. Recommend how to discover the endpoint, authenticate, execute SQL, and know when downstream tasks can start. Our DAGs may be delivered from Git or S3, and their Python code needs the DataLens SDK to look up platform resources. Explain how to make the SDK available in either deployment. Do not call APIs or deploy anything.
evals.expected_output: Use the native Trino endpoint discovered through getTrinoCluster for both Git-managed ETL and unsaved diagnostics, authenticate with a Yandex Cloud IAM bearer token, and submit statements sequentially, waiting for each to succeed before starting the next or releasing dependent tasks. Explain the current saved-query API limitation and make the SDK plus dependencies importable through the selected DAG deployment or supported package installation.

assertions.text: Chooses direct Trino execution for both Git-managed ETL and the temporary diagnostic; discovers coordinatorUrl through /rpc/getTrinoCluster or its documented SDK equivalent.
Specifies a Yandex Cloud IAM token in Authorization: Bearer for the Trino endpoint, without embedding or logging a real token.

Submits one SQL statement at a time via /v1/statement in file order, follows nextUri until absent and checks errors before submitting the next statement or releasing downstream tasks; does not submit the multi-statement file as one request.
Explains that the public DataLens SQL-query API currently runs a saved query by ID and does not invent a raw-SQL argument or a temporary-query RPC.

Recommends making the DataLens SDK available with DAGs delivered from Git or S3, ensures dependencies and imports work in the parser and workers, and does not treat uploading an uninstalled archive as sufficient.
